title.rendered: Single-Minded: Ask in Faith Without Doubting: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Ask in faith, without doubting. The double-minded person is unstable in all they do. The Christian life is not won by hedging. It is won by leaning the whole weight of the heart in one direction.

content.rendered:
Ask in faith, without doubting. The double-minded person is unstable in all they do. The Christian life is not won by hedging. It is won by leaning the whole weight of the heart in one direction.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, June 25, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to you. But when you ask, you must believe and not doubt, because the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind. That person should not expect to receive anything from the Lord. Such a person is double-minded and unstable in all they do.”
James 1:5-8 (NIV)

Today’s Message

James gives one of the most generous promises in the New Testament. If anyone lacks wisdom, ask God. He gives generously. Without finding fault. And it will be given. Then he adds the condition that has unsettled many believers since. Ask in faith, without doubting. The one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.

It is important to read the next phrase carefully. James calls the doubter “double-minded.” The Greek is dipsuchos. Literally “two-souled.” It does not mean someone who has questions or who wrestles with their faith. It means someone whose heart is divided between two masters, two systems, two loyalties. They want to believe God. They also want to keep their options open. They ask God for wisdom while half-trusting another source. They pray for help while still trying to engineer the outcome themselves. They look at the Lord with one eye while the other eye is fixed on the world. That is double-mindedness.

The wave of the sea image is exact. A wave is shaped by every wind. It cannot hold a position. It is moved by whatever pressure is strongest at the moment. The double-minded believer is the same. They cannot commit. They cannot trust. They cannot stand in any belief long enough for it to bear fruit. James says, plainly, that such a person should not expect to receive anything from the Lord. Not because God is harsh. Because the double-minded heart cannot receive what God wants to give.

The cure is not more religion. The cure is single-mindedness. Lean the whole weight of your heart in one direction. Ask God, and then actually trust Him. Pray, and then actually wait on the answer. Commit to the path the Spirit is showing you, and then walk it without looking back. The believer who lives this way is the believer in whom God can begin to work, deeply, over decades.

So today, audit your heart. Where are you double-minded? Where have you been asking God for wisdom while still trying to control the outcome yourself? Where have you been praying for help while still trusting a backup plan more than you trust the Lord? Repent of the division. Lean fully. And watch what God begins to do in a heart that has chosen one master.

Prayer

Father, I confess where I have been double-minded. Where I have asked You for help while still trying to control the outcome. Where I have prayed for direction while still trusting a backup plan more than I trusted You. Cleanse my divided heart. Make me single-minded. Anchor me in You alone. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am not double-minded. I am not a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by every wind. I lean the whole weight of my heart on the Lord. I ask in faith. I receive in faith. My heart is committed to one Master, Jesus Christ.
